title: GCSE, level 1 and 2 results 2026 at a glance: key trends and context for teachers

content.text: More than 5.7 million GCSE results have been issued to students in England today, along with more than 374,000 results for level 1 and 2 vocational and technical qualifications (VTQs).

These results allow young people to progress to the next stage of their lives, whatever that may be. They represent a great deal of hard work on the part of students, teachers, and schools, as well as parents and carers. Congratulations to all.
This year’s GCSE results are stable overall in comparison with those in 2025. Small variations, either up or down, are normal from year to year and from subject to subject.
GCSE results: what teachers need to know
Level 1 and 2 vocational and technical qualification (VTQ) results: what teachers need to know
Results for 363,210 technical awards have been issued today, up very slightly on last year’s figure.
Results for 11,185 technical certificates have been shared today with post-16s across England, down 10% on last year’s figure.
The standard of work required to achieve each grade in these qualifications has remained consistent.
Where to find more details about GCSE and level 1 and 2 results
For a more detailed look into all of our data take a look at our statistical report on this year’s results and our interactive outcomes charts.
Amanda Swann, Executive Director for Delivery, Ofqual
